$comment: The single source of truth for what CI runs, and for what it deliberately does not.
Specs in this repository are partitioned across 40 Playwright configs, each of which
encodes real requirements for its tier: roles.setup dependencies, a 300s chain timeout,
a different storageState. Re-deriving all that into one mega-config would lose those
details quietly. So CI runs the configs themselves, and this file lists which ones.
The danger with a hand-maintained list is that it goes stale in silence: a spec is
written, nothing CI runs collects it, and it never executes while still looking covered.
That had already happened. tests/ranges-discover.spec.ts was listed in modules.config.ts
as owned by all-tc.config.ts, which does not collect it; the only config that did was a
scratch probe bucket nobody runs. It was excluded on the strength of a claim that was
never true, and executed by no one.
scripts/check-ci-coverage.mjs reads this file, asks Playwright which files each listed
config actually resolves, and fails if any spec in the tree is run by nobody and has no
recorded reason. Note that this is NOT the same question as scripts/check-orphans.mjs,
which asks whether a spec is reachable by SOME config. That gate was passing cleanly on
2026-09-12 while this workflow ran 2 of 40 configs, 69 of 227 spec files.
So: to add a spec, put it in a config listed in `suites`. To deliberately keep one out
of CI, add it to `excluded` with a reason. There is no third option that passes.

This said capture.config.ts until 2026-09-12, which collects ONE root spec and not a
single file under tests/docs. `suite: docs` would have run one capture spec and reported
success. Caught by dry-running the shard filter rather than by reading the manifest,
which is the same lesson as everything else in this file: ask the tool what it resolves.

$shards: A single job cannot hold them. Run 34656118535 was cancelled at the 90-minute job cap
with modules.config.ts ALONE still running after 79 minutes, and that was 1 of 28 configs.
A cancelled run produces no verdict at all, which is the one outcome worse than a red one.
Each shard is a separate job that boots its own stack (~10 min, mostly the healthcheck
wait) and runs its slice. That buys parallel wall clock at the cost of repeating the boot,
which is the right trade when the suites dominate by an order of magnitude.
1  modules          the flat tests/ sweep, 43 files, the heaviest single config
2  regression-chains  26 chains at a 300s timeout each
3  the long tail that still takes real time: all-tc, deep, guards, e2e, ...
4  everything else, most of which is one or two files
Shards are assigned EXPLICITLY rather than round-robined, because the configs differ in
cost by two orders of magnitude and an automatic split would put modules and chains in the
same job half the time. scripts/check-ci-coverage.mjs validates that every suite has a
shard in range, so a new config cannot be added without deciding where it goes.
Rebalance by editing the numbers here. Nothing else needs to change.
